reasonToGo: Driftholt's crossing ground. The col and the saddle here are the only walked way between one coast of the island and the other, and the meadow that carries them is the widest on the landmass — 94.8 per cent of this region against 91.4 and 95.2 on the other two walked ones. A party comes over it for the grazing on either side, for what the marsh yields at the edges, and for the cut platform, which is the only stone this ground offers and the only stone on Driftholt that anyone has walked to.

hazards.name: The notch wind
hazards.description: Everything crossing the island is funnelled through one saddle and comes out of it at a pitch nothing on either coast prepares a party for. A crew caught in the notch with a load goes down and stays down until it drops, which is usually hours and occasionally a day.

hazards.name: The tectonic cave
hazards.description: The cave under the cuesta is a split in the rock and not a cut by water: it has no floor to speak of, it narrows without warning, and it goes further back than the light does. What is known about it is the first hundred paces.

resources.name: Saddle grain
resources.description: Sown on the sheltered flanks either side of the col, where the meadow is deep and the notch wind goes over rather than through. It is the only tilled ground drawn on Driftholt and it feeds the crossing rather than any settlement, because there is no settlement on this region.

resources.name: Marsh greens
resources.description: Gathered off the marsh strip at the tidal flat and the estuary head, which is a twentieth of this ground and the whole of its green food. It is taken between tides and eaten the same day; nothing here keeps.

resources.name: Platform flag
resources.description: Levered off the cut platform where the sea has already loosened the bedding, and carried up whole. It is the only stone worked anywhere on Driftholt: the island draws no rock, no scree and no karst in any of its eight regions, so what is not prised off the platform does not exist.

landmarks.name: Withyshallow Saddle
landmarks.description: The notch through the ridge, and with the col below it the only crossing between Driftholt's two coasts that anyone has walked. It is bare, it is short, and in the wrong weather it is impassable for days at a time.

landmarks.name: Geo at Merefall
landmarks.description: The cleft at the seaward foot of the crossing, with the arch standing outside it and the drowned valley running in behind. Boats lie in it while a party is over the saddle, because there is nowhere else on this coast to lie.
